instruments.name: Remission/Normal Stool Frequency (SF)
instruments.recall_period: the number of stools in a 24-hour period when the participant was in remission or, if the participant has never achieved remission, the reported SF before initial onset of signs and symptoms of UC
instruments.mode: recorded electronically as source data at the screening study visit
instruments.purpose: reference “normal” SF used with the participant-reported daily SF to calculate the Mayo SF subscore
soa_activities: Site staff explains, participant reports remission/normal stool frequency

evidence.quote: The Normal SF is a participant-reported measure. This item reports the number of stools in a 24-hour period when the participant was in remission or, if the participant has never achieved remission, the reported SF before initial onset of signs and symptoms of UC.
The participant will record this electronically as source data at the screening study visit.
Note: The “Remission/Normal Stool Frequency (SF)” question should be explained to the participant before the participant answers the question
Study software will use the participant-reported daily SF and the reference normal SF to automatically calculate the Mayo SF subscore.
The purpose of UC remission question should be explained before the participant answers the question.

Stool Frequency: The SF subscore is a participant-reported measure. This item reports the number of stools in a 24-hour period, relative to the normal number of stools for that participant in the same period, on a 4-point scale.
The total number of stools passed in a 24-hour period will be recorded by the participant in a daily eDiary.

instruments.recall_period: during the night (or day, for shift workers)

evidence.quote: Nocturnal Stool: The Nocturnal Stool instrument is a single item asking the participant to record the number of stools they had during the night (or day, for shift workers) causing them to waken from sleep.
Participants will be provided with an electronic diary tool during screening to record information daily pertaining to their nocturnal stool count.

Bristol Stool Scale: The Bristol Stool Scale is a single item that provides a pictorial and verbal description of stool consistency and form ranging from Type 1 (Hard Lumps) to Type 7 (Watery/liquid).

Urgency NRS: A single item that measures the severity for the urgency (sudden or immediate need) to have a bowel movement in the past 24 hours using an 11-point NRS ranging from 0 (no urgency) to 10 (worst possible urgency).

Abdominal Pain NRS: A single item that measures the “worst abdominal pain in the past 24 hours” using an 11-point NRS ranging from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst possible pain).

instruments.name: Patient’s Global Rating of Severity
instruments.purpose: to assess the patients’ rating of their disease symptom severity

evidence.quote: Patient’s Global Rating of Severity (PGR-S): The PGR-S is a 1-item patient-rated questionnaire designed to assess the patients’ rating of their disease symptom severity over the past 24 hours. Responses are graded on a 6-point scale in which a score of 1 indicates the
participant has no symptoms (that is, “none”) and a score of 6 indicates that the participant’s symptom(s) are “very severe.”

evidence.quote: The QIDS-SR16 is a self-administered, 16-item instrument intended to assess the existence and severity of symptoms of depression
A participant is asked to consider each statement as it relates to the way he or she has felt for the past 7 days.
The 16 items corresponding to 9 depression domains are summed to give a single score ranging from 0 to 27, with higher scores denoting greater symptom severity.
The QIDS-SR16 data will be collected via a tablet device and/or a web-based collection system.

notes: Extracted from Protocol J1P-MC-KFAH(b) (Amendment b, approval date 03-Jun-2021), the only protocol version in the PDF; the SoA notes are on its pages 17-46, so no later amendment applies. The page 4 document-history table lists Amendment (a) 18 November 2020 and Original Protocol 03 September 2020 only as history; their text is not in the PDF. Text layer: many pages (e.g. 18, 21-23, 43-45, 84, 86-89, 122-125, 146-147, 150) have a letter-spaced text layer ('C O N FI D E N TI A L'); quotes and abbreviations from those pages are copied as the text layer has them (spacing preserved, so the checker can find them), which makes those abbreviation terms read e.g. 'F S H'. No page reads '[no text layer on this page]'. Rule 10: the lab-tests table pages 120, 122, 123 and 124 were checked on the page image. The images confirm that 'TB test based on local standard of care' is the note on the Tuberculosis (TB) test row, and that on page 124 'Results will not be provided to the investigative sites.' belongs to a redacted (CCI) row of the Stool Samples table, not to Clostridium difficile testing; 'Endoscopic biopsy sample collection' on page 124 is the note of a fully redacted panel. Redacted (CCI) panels/rows on pages 122 (Additional Testing analyte), 123 and 124 are not recorded as analytes; 'Additional Testing' is kept with an empty analyte list. Abbreviations: Appendix 12 (pages 145-150) in full, plus abbreviations printed under the SoA tables (page 23: AESIs, SoA, V; defined there differently or not in Appendix 12) and under the hypersensitivity lab table (page 125: LY, NMH). Other abbreviation footnotes (pages 82, 94, 95, 143 and SoA pages 32, 42, 46) repeat Appendix 12 terms and are not duplicated. Small differences: SoA note (vital signs) says vital signs should be measured after sitting at least 5 minutes, Section 8.2.1 says blood pressure and pulse rate; Lipid panel SoA note says fasting samples are preferred, Appendix 2 says no food or drink except water for 12 hours before the test (nonfasting not a deviation); TB test: SoA note says central or local laboratory, Appendix 2 gives QuantiFERON (Lilly-designated), T-SPOT.TB (local), TST (local). Serum pregnancy: Section 8.2.5.1 says central laboratory, Appendix 2 'Lilly-designated laboratory'. Flow cytometry panel: Appendix 2 lists T regulatory cells and T-cell subsets; Section 8.6 (PD biomarkers include changes in T-cell subsets) does not name the SoA row, so no purpose is recorded. Geboes score is recorded as an instrument without an SoA activity (the text ties it to biopsies and histologic endpoints, not to an SoA row by name). SoA rows not described in the text beyond the SoA itself: Informed consent, Demographics, medical-history rows, Prior treatments, Concomitant medications, Tobacco use, Alcohol and caffeine use, Patient diary dispensed, Diary return, Randomization, Dosing; five rows are redacted as 'CCI'. Tokens in SoA activity names not defined in the abbreviation list: 'CCI' (redaction marker, 6 rows). The SoA note T2:c30 is bound to 'Endoscopic Procedure', which is an SoA section header, not an activity in soa_activities.
